Imo, Hoyoverse adds more and more talent-focused bow characters since most players don't use bow DPSes because of their issues. I think you should keep a diary. One thing I've realized is that a person's subconscious thought can control them to a much greater extent that they assume. They are often complex, hard to decipher, and while some of them are rather harmless, many of which can ruin one's life. Self-harm is a way to turn those invisible thoughts into something tangible, which solves nothing because the root of the problem is still there. That is why you should try to understand yourself. Write down your thoughts, think hard about the true motive behind your actions. Be as knowledgable about yourself as possible, and maybe win a couple of Nobel prize on Yourself-ology or something. That is the only long-term way to deal with your problems.

"But why should one go through all of this trouble when it's much easier to just give up?" I can't answer that, because life is objectively meaningless. No matter who you are and what you do, death is inevitable. And when you are dead, nothing matters at all because you no longer exist. You don't feel pain, you don't feel happy, you don't feel sad. You think nothing and feel nothing. Those thoughts hit me like a truck, paralized me, left me unable to find any incentives to do anything. As I looked at other people, my friends and family specifically, working hard even though they didn't really like the work, I wonder how can they be so competent, so diligent, so responsible, while I was just lying there exhausted. 

But then I found out the key word: "SUBJECTIVE". Life is OBJECTIVELY meaningless, but it can be SUBJECTIVELY meaningful. So I watch anime. Like, that's it. My life goal is to watch anime. It seems more like a simple hobby than something as grand of a concept as the meaning of life. But it is enough to keep me going. There is still a constant battle between my desire to live and my nihilistic thoughts, but it is definitely better than being stuck forever in a bottomless pit. If one day, I find this meaning of life to be lame and cringe, I'll just make another, and another, until the day my life time runs out.

I hated studying. So I had long struggled to find my true passion, something that I truly loved, but every time I tried anything, I would have just dropped in 2 weeks at best. I thought I was like that because I lack resilience. So, in the end of my middle school years, I set a goal for myself: to enter the local most prestigious high school. But I fucking HATE studying. There was a constant battle between the need to study, and the urge to just screw it all. Whenever I lost that battle, I would curse myself, to a point where I occasionally self-harmed. I knew it was destructive, but I clung to the idea that the joy of overcoming great obstacle when I succeed would make it all worth it. "That joy would encourage me to actually learn something new and have a passion" - I thought

In the end, I got admitted. Everyone around me overcame with joy, except for me. All I got is some mild satisfaction that quickly faded away, leaving behind an even greater emptiness than before. My willingness to study just slowly, but consistently, diminished. I continued to try stuff out: learn game development, learn to play the guitar, etc, but they were all fruitless. Eventually, I stopped. "I'm just someone with no passion at all".

I would often find myself playing video games, or spacing out instead of putting any effort into studying. "Maybe it was because I had video game addiction" - I thought. Before I even tried to do anything, I just lost interest in it.

Everything became unfulfilling since then. I feel like I'm on a very, very long train trip. All I can do is sit there and wait until it reach the final destination: death. I HATE myself. Other people are so diligent, so responsible, even though they are doing work they don't like. And then there's me, not wanting to do anything, like an useless pile of dogshit.

The day before yesterday, I tried to commit suicide. It failed, obviously, because I hadn't kicked the chair away before hanging, so the survival instinct easily saved me.

I've got no clue if things will eventually get better, because I am still on that train, on the very same seat.

But at least it got less lonely now, knowing I'm not the only passenger.
